caption: What a Git commit really stores: snapshots, trees and blobs, not diffs.

problem.narration: At the core of Git is a simple key-value data store. A commit does not hold a diff. It specifies the top-level tree for the snapshot of the project at that point. Trees match folders, and blobs hold file contents. So each commit points to a full picture of the project, not a list of changes.

fix.narration: So where do deltas come from? Only from saving space. Conceptually there are only four object types: commit, tree, tag and blob. But to save space, an object can be stored as a delta of another base object. That happens in pack files.

summary.narration: Three objects. A commit is a snapshot of the project. A tree is a folder. A blob is the content of a file.

outro.narration: If you wondered how Git works inside, there are more breakdowns on elvaric.
